 Follow St. Louis man sentenced to 17 years in prison for child sex crime
 Jacob Kuerth Mon, November 2, 2026 at 12:59 AM UTC 1 min read Add Yahoo as a preferred source to see more of our stories on Google. stock.adobe.com A 33-year-old man was sentenced Thursday to 17 years in prison after a jury found him guilty of sexually abusing a young girl in St. Louis' Mark Twain neighborhood.
 Ricky Young was convicted of statutory sodomy involving a child younger than 12, according to the St. Louis Circuit Attorney's Office.
 Police began investigating the allegations in April 2022 after receiving a report of a sexual assault involving a minor.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement According to prosecutors, an 8-year-old girl was playing a game called "ten fingers" with her siblings in a car. During the game, the children were asked questions and instructed to put down a finger if their answer was yes.
 When asked whether an adult had ever touched them, the girl identified Young.
 During a subsequent forensic interview at the Child Advocacy Center, the girl said Young had forced her to perform a sexual act on him when she was 5 or 6 years old.
 "When an adult abuses a position of trust to exploit a child, the harm extends far beyond a single moment," Circuit Attorney Gabe Gore said in a statement. "(The) sentence ensures the defendant is held accountable for his actions and reflects our commitment to protecting the most vulnerable members of our community."
